title: A study to find out whether a remouldable prosthetic socket is acceptable and practical for people who have had a below-knee amputation and are being fitted with their first prosthesis
official: ASSIST: A randomised feasibility trial to assess the Acceptability of a remouldable Socket System in the Immediate rehabilitation phase of people with a tranSTibial amputation
summary:
Background and study aims 
When someone has a below-knee amputation, they may be offered an artificial leg (prosthesis) to help them stand, walk and move around. The prosthesis is attached to the remaining part of the leg (called the residual limb) using a specially made socket. At the moment, most sockets are made using a plaster cast of the residual limb. The socket is then manufactured, which can take around 3-4 weeks. During the first year after an amputation, the shape and size of the residual limb can change as swelling reduces and muscles change. This can mean that several new sockets are needed, causing further delays and hospital appointments.
The ASSIST study will look at a new type of socket called a remouldable socket. This socket can be heated and reshaped to fit changes in the size and shape of the residual limb, rather than making a completely new socket each time.
The study aims to find out whether it is possible and acceptable to carry out a larger research study to compare the remouldable sockets with the usual NHS sockets.
In particular, this study will look at:
1. Whether people are willing to take part in the study and be randomly allocated to one of two types of socket;
2. Whether the remouldable socket is acceptable to people using it;
3. Whether the study procedures and assessments work well;
4. Whether it is possible to collect information about quality of life, comfort, mobility, adjustment to the prosthesis and healthcare costs;
5. How patients and healthcare professionals feel about the study and how it could be improved.
The findings will help researchers decide if a larger study should be carried out to find out whether remouldable sockets offer benefits to patients and value for money for the NHS.

Who can participate? 
Patients aged 18 years or older who have had a below-knee amputation, are waiting to receive their first prosthesis, are expected to be able to walk using a prosthesis, and are receiving physiotherapy at one of the participating prosthetics centres or its associated community rehabilitation service.

What does the study involve? 
Participants are expected to be involved in the study for approximately 5 months. They will be randomly allocated to one of two groups, with an equal chance of being allocated to either group:
1. Remouldable socket group:  participants will receive a remouldable socket. This socket can be heated and reshaped as the size and shape of residual limb changes.
2. Usual care group:  participants will receive the standard NHS socket, which is made using the usual plaster-casting and manufacturing process.
All participants will continue to receive usual physiotherapy and rehabilitation throughout their participation in the study regardless of group allocation.
There will be four main study visits, which will take place during usual routine appointments:
1. First appointment – before the socket is made: The study team will check the participant is eligible to take part, ask them to answer some questions about their quality of life, and collect information about their health and mobility.
2. Second appointment – when the socket is cast: The residual limb will be measured and cast for the allocated type of socket and the participant will be asked some questions about their quality of life.
3. Third appointment – 2 months after socket casting: Participants will be asked to complete some questionnaires and take part in a simple mobility test.
4. Fourth appointment – 4 months after socket casting: Participants will repeat the questionnaires and mobility test, and will also be asked to rate any changes in their quality of life, socket comfort, ease of movement using the prosthesis and adjustment to using the prosthesis, during study participation.
The questionnaires will ask about:
1. General health and quality of life
2. How comfortable the socket is
3. How easy it is to move around using the prosthesis
4. Feelings about adjusting to life with the prosthesis
5. Any healthcare appointments or services used
Some participants will also be invited to take part in an interview to talk about their experiences of the study and, where relevant, using the remouldable socket. Taking part in an interview is optional.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Taking part in the study may provide some potential benefits, although these cannot be guaranteed. Possible benefits for participants allocated to the remouldable socket group include receiving their prosthesis more quickly; having a socket that can be adjusted as the shape and size of the residual limb changes; potentially needing fewer replacement sockets and appointments; and improved socket comfort and mobility. Taking part will also help researchers understand how best to support people following an amputation and improve prosthetic services for future patients.
Patients with a below-knee amputation who are using a new prosthesis may all experience falls, blistering due to wearing the prosthetic limb or skin damage to the remaining limb or foot. The chance of experiencing one of these events is not increased by taking part in the study. There is a small chance participants in the remouldable socket group might experience a skin reaction to the silicone liner. This would be managed as per usual care by the clinical team.
Taking part will involve completing some short questionnaires and study assessments. There is a possibility that answering some of the questions may cause distress. Participants do not have to answer all of the questions and will be supported by the research team.

Where is the study run from?
The host NHS organisation is Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust and the lead research organisation is the University of Hull. The study is coordinated by Hull Health Trials Unit (UK).

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
1 July 2026 to 30 June 2028, with recruitment expected to open from January 2027.

Who is funding the study?
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

Who is the main contact? 
Prof. Natalie Vanicek, n.vanicek@hull.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients will be included if they:
1. Have a major unilateral below-knee amputation, of any aetiology
2. Are awaiting their first prosthesis
3. Are expected to ambulate with a prosthesis, as measured with the Amputee Mobility Predictor
4. Are receiving physiotherapy at the limb-fitting centre or in the community at the main primary continuing care sites
5. Are able to provide informed consent
6. Are willing to trial remouldable socket in case they are randomised into that group
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded if they:
1. Have a life-limiting illness unrelated to amputation
2. Have a bulbous residual limb at the time of casting (circumference at distal end is >2 cm compared to circumference at tibial tuberosity) as it may not be possible to fit the remouldable socket if the participant is randomised into that group
3. Have a body mass greater than 80 kg with a distal circumference of 16-23 cm (small socket) OR have a body mass greater than 125 kg with a distal circumference of 20-38 cm (medium socket)
4. Have a residual limb greater than 27 cm as per manufacturer’s recommendations
5. Are receiving physiotherapy in the community OUTSIDE OF the primary continuing care sites 
6. Have any contraindication to wearing a silicone liner
7. Have severe upper limb dysfunction (due to strength requirement to don/doff the silicone liner)
8. Have a known allergy to silicone liner and/or inability to visually inspect the residual limb by themselves or with the help of a caregiver (in case of allergic reaction to silicone liner)
9. Have a disease affecting memory (Abbreviated Mental Test Score of 3 or less, indicative of severe impairment)
